citation.authors: Rudnicka AR, Mt-Isa S, Owen CG, Cook DG et al

record.population: 46 studies of open-angle glaucoma prevalence: 103,567 participants, 2,509 cases
record.design: Bayesian meta-analysis of observational prevalence studies by age, gender and race
record.finding: Black populations had the highest prevalence of primary open-angle glaucoma at all ages, though the proportional rise with age was steepest in white populations. Estimated prevalence above age 70 was 6% in white, 16% in black and 3% in Asian populations. Men were 1.37 times more likely than women to have it.
record.note: Studies from many countries; race categories as in the original studies; authors in London.
